sample.description:
Many Americans took advantage of historically low mortgage rates during the pandemic. But for homeowners who opted for adjustable-rate mortgages, those savings might not last. As mortgage rates continue to remain elevated, hundreds of thousands of borrowers are soon nearing the end of their introductory fixed-rate periods, putting them at risk of higher monthly payments. And with refinancing no longer offering the same relief it once did, some homeowners could find themselves facing a difficult financial decision.

sample.title: LIVE: Reuters NEXT Newsmaker with Japan minister Minoru Kiuchi
sample.description:
Japan is at a pivotal moment in its economy. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government is pursuing an ambitious agenda to revitalize growth through investment while also facing pressure to restore fiscal health. Policymakers are grappling with a weaker yen, rising government borrowing costs and growing scrutiny from financial markets over the sustainability of Japan's public finances. 

Kiuchi is tasked with helping shape the administration's strategy to boost Japan's long-term growth potential while maintaining confidence in its fiscal framework — in an economy emerging from decades of low inflation and sluggish growth.

Reuters Chief Correspondent, Japan Markets, Rocky Swift will sit down with Kiuchi at LSEG Insight Tokyo to discuss the government's approach and the outlook for Japan's economy, including the challenges and opportunities facing the country amid shifting global economic conditions and heightened volatility in financial markets.

Pope Leo’s doctors give update on his condition | BBC News
sample.description:
Pope Leo XIV's recovery from surgery to remove a lower lobe of his lung is "progressing as expected", his doctors have said.
 
The 71-year-old pontiff has started to walk and has "resumed a normal diet" following the roughly 90-minute procedure, the medics said in an update shared by the Vatican.
 
The Pope was diagnosed with lung cancer after the surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, which the Vatican said had been "successful" and proceeded without complications.
 
Blood tests and an X-ray early on Wednesday showed his recovery was "proceeding normally", the doctors said, and he has also undergone respiratory physiotherapy.
 
The pontiff is expected to remain there for about a week as he recovers.
